title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 60
paragraphs: As for the number each separate nation supplied, I cannot give exact information, since none of my sources give it; but the total of the whole land army proved to be one million seven hundred thousand. They counted them as follows. They gathered together in one place a body of ten thousand men and packed them as tightly as they could, then drew a circle around them on the outside. Having drawn the circle and let the ten thousand go, they built a wall of loose stones around the circumference, rising to a man's navel. Having done this, they made others enter the walled space, until in this way they had counted them all. After counting them, they organized them by nations.
